newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--OTE's second share offer will test the waters today in a try-out of the course of the capital market. From indications last week the capital market is moving to the rhythms of the OTE offer which the state hopes will raise 450 billion drachmas for the state-run organisation's share capital increase.

--The Bank of Greece is recommending that firms lend in Ecu to avoid the unrest plaguing the yen. Ecu loans will avert the dangers associated with forex lending, the banks says, and an added guarantee is Greece's stable exchange policy keeping the drachma on a stable parity with the Ecu.

--There's concern in the government's economic team over the course of inflation and prices, indicated by the finance ministry's decision to abandon original plans for monthly auctions of fixed-rate bonds.

--The finance ministry will reschedule the 1.5 trillion drachmas in debts owed to the state, through a new bill that foresees the drastic reduction of all fines on tax debts. The new code that will be effective for debts from now on will be "realistic" as well as punitive.

--The state itself bears much of the responsibility for the overwhelming amount of money owed to IKA, the social security foundation. Of an estimated one trillion drachmas outstanding, more thana 50 billion are owed by state enterprises, organisations, ministries and municipalities.

--Intracome, Greece's leading telecoms firm, sees a good result in 1997, with sales of 55-60 billion drachmas and profits up by 20 percent over 1996 at 8.5 billion drachmas. Exports are expected to total 16-17 billion drachmas.

--Industry has seen an explosive rise in turnover and profits. In retail sales, the ten largest names increased their turnover by 175 billion drachmas - 23 percent - although profits stabilised or fell marginally.

--Work begins on the Elefsina-Stavros-Spata international airport highway this month, following the finalisation of guarantees from commercial banks on the granting of a loan from the European Investment Bank.
--Taxation of firms in Greece is among the highest in Europe while income tax on individuals is among the lowest, according to a new study.

--The lack of fluidity on the market which has caused an increase in interest on bond sales, in combination with aggressive OTE and banking share sales led the bourse to significant losses last week. The Bank of Greece is expected to intervene this week to normalise fluidity and the course of interest rates. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
